blurb:
If you've got someone in your house under 25, they already know who Yeat is. If you're the one buying the tickets, consider this your crash course: he's one of the most streamed artists in rap right now, known for a sound that's dense, layered, and loud in the best possible way.

He hits the Coca-Cola Roxy on Tuesday, September 22nd. The Roxy is an ideal room for this kind of show, big enough to feel like an event, intimate enough to actually feel the bass. If you've been looking for a reason to introduce someone younger to a real concert experience, or if you already know every word, either way this one delivers.

Get tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Yeat skews younger than the median Perimeter Post reader at 38, but the audience has a young professional segment and likely parents of teens/young adults. The Roxy is a familiar, accessible venue. Lower demographic fit than Chelsea Handler or Suki Waterhouse, but still a legitimate one-night concert worth surfacing.

event_name: To The Limit: The Ultimate Eagles Experience
blurb:
The Eagles catalog is one of those things that sounds like it belongs in an elevator until you're actually hearing 'Hotel California' or 'Desperado' live in a real room, and then it hits completely differently. To The Limit is a nationally touring Eagles tribute act with a reputation for doing this right, not a local bar cover band doing their best, but a group that's played prestigious theaters around the country and has built a real following doing exactly this.

They're at The Strand Theatre in Marietta on Friday, October 2nd. The Strand is a beautiful historic venue on the Square, and it's the right size for a show like this: close enough to feel it, big enough to be a proper event. VIP tickets are available and include early access, a pre-show mini-concert, meet and greet, two drink tickets, and a signed poster. The VIP window opens at 6:30pm, lobby for regular admission at 7pm, showtime at 8.

For empty nesters or anyone who grew up with these songs in heavy rotation, this is a great Friday night.
scoring_notes: The Eagles demographic skews toward the 45-65 empty nester portion of the Perimeter Post audience. The Strand is a well-loved local venue with strong goodwill. Tribute acts are not rare, but To The Limit has a national touring profile which lifts the uniqueness score. VIP package adds a premium tier that fits the $105K HHI audience well.

event_name: Tapestry Tunes: A Carole King Tribute Cabaret
blurb:
The Tapestry album came out in 1971. It sat at number one for six straight years. If you grew up hearing 'You've Got a Friend' or 'I Feel the Earth Move,' you didn't just hear those songs, you felt them. They're the kind of thing that sticks.

On Sunday, September 27th, The Alley Stage on the Marietta Square is hosting Tapestry Tunes, a Carole King tribute cabaret featuring Bethany Irby, who recently played the lead in Aurora Theatre's 'Beautiful: The Carole King Musical.' This isn't a cover band at a bar. Irby is the real deal, a trained vocalist with 20 years of Atlanta stage credits, and the cabaret format means it's an intimate, close-up experience that a big theatre production can't replicate.

This one is great for empty nesters or anyone looking for a genuinely warm night out that doesn't require earplugs. Grab tickets soon, a show like this in a small room fills up fast.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the empty nester segment of the Perimeter Post audience. Carole King's catalog has broad generational appeal across 40-65 year olds. Cabaret format in a small venue adds intimacy and uniqueness. Slightly lower demographic fit for younger readers, but the mixed audience skew means this serves a real slice of the readership.

event_name: Guided Tasting & Tour at ASW Distillery
blurb:
ASW Distillery sits right in the Battery area and makes some genuinely award-winning craft gin and vodka. On Sunday, September 27th, they're running a guided tasting and tour: four pours led by one of their experienced guides, followed by a behind-the-scenes look at how the spirits are distilled on their copper hybrid still.

The whole thing runs about 90 minutes and starts at 2pm, which makes it a natural anchor for an afternoon. Grab brunch beforehand, do the tour, and you've got a complete Sunday without driving all over town. For couples or small groups who want something a little more interesting than a restaurant, this is a solid call.

They ask you to arrive 15 minutes early for parking and check-in. You can grab a drink while you wait, which is a very reasonable policy.
scoring_notes: Distillery tours run regularly, so uniqueness is moderate, but the demographic fit is strong for the Perimeter Post's educated, $105K HHI, adult-leaning readership. ASW is a well-regarded local brand and the Battery location is familiar territory for this audience. Good pairing activity for couples and small groups. Weekday casual tone works for Sunday afternoon framing.

venue: The Block at You42 Studios, Metro Atlanta
blurb:
BONNIE X CLYDE are bringing their festival sound to The Block at You42 Studios for a one-night-only 360° Boiler Room-style show on Friday, September 25th. The format alone is worth paying attention to: instead of a traditional stage setup, the crowd surrounds the performance from all sides, which turns a concert into something closer to a real shared experience.

BONNIE X CLYDE have been a fixture at major electronic music festivals for years, known for a high-energy, genre-blending set that doesn't really have an off switch. If you've been to one of those festivals and thought 'I wish I could just see them in a smaller room,' this is that night.

Doors at 9pm, runs to 2am. This is a late-night pick, not a dinner-and-home situation. But for the right crowd, it's the kind of Friday that makes the rest of the weekend feel earned.
scoring_notes: The 360° Boiler Room format is genuinely unique and differentiates this from a standard club night. Skews toward the younger professional segment of the Perimeter Post audience. Late-night start (9pm to 2am) limits appeal for families and older empty nesters, but for young professionals this is a standout pick. Uniqueness score is high because the format itself is rare locally.

blurb:
Suki Waterhouse has been quietly building one of the more interesting careers in indie pop. She started releasing music in 2016, spent years developing a dreamy, understated sound, and then her song 'Good Looking' blew up in a way that felt genuinely earned rather than manufactured. Now she's on a real tour, and she's stopping at the Coca-Cola Roxy on Tuesday, September 29th.

This is the kind of show that sells out and then people are annoyed they missed it. The Roxy is a great room for her vibe, not too big, good sound, and the Battery area gives you plenty of dinner options before the show if you want to make a full night of it.

Tickets are available now. Don't wait on this one.
scoring_notes: Waterhouse fits well with the 38 median age, educated, adult-leaning Perimeter Post reader. She has crossover appeal between younger millennials and older Gen Z. One-night concert at a premium venue, and her recent surge in popularity makes this feel timely and relevant. Strong pick for young professionals and couples looking for a night out.

venue: Mimms Museum of Technology and Art, Roswell
blurb:
Randy Wigginton helped write the software for the Apple II and the original Macintosh. After that he went on to shape things at eBay, Google, Square, and Block. He's been at the center of basically every major wave in modern computing, and on Saturday, September 19th, he's going to sit down at the Mimms Museum of Technology and Art in Roswell and just... tell you about it.

For a room full of people who work in tech, manage teams that run on tech, or are raising kids who will eventually inherit all of this, that's a pretty compelling two hours. These are not TED Talk-style highlights either. This is a guy with five decades of firsthand stories, including the people, the breakthroughs, and the moments that didn't go according to plan.

The Mimms Museum is a gem of a venue that a lot of locals haven't been to yet. This is a good reason to fix that. Details and tickets are on their site.
scoring_notes: Perimeter Post skews toward highly educated ($105K HHI, 70% bachelor's+), tech-adjacent professionals. Randy Wigginton's resume (Apple II, Mac, Google, eBay) is DIRECTLY relevant to this audience. One-time speaking event at a niche museum venue adds uniqueness. High intellectual interest match. Strong pick.

blurb:
Chelsea Handler does not do polite. She does honest, unfiltered, and genuinely funny in a way that makes you laugh out loud and then feel slightly guilty about it. And she's bringing that exact energy to the Coca-Cola Roxy on Friday, October 2nd.

This is a real stand-up night out, not a panel or a podcast taping or some watered-down speaking event. Handler has been doing this for 20+ years and she gets sharper with age. If you've got a group of friends who are overdue for a proper evening that doesn't involve a kid's soccer schedule or a work happy hour, this is your excuse.

Tickets are moving. Grab yours now before you're stuck watching the highlights on someone else's Instagram story.
scoring_notes: Chelsea Handler skews perfectly toward the Perimeter Post audience: educated, adult-leaning, $105K household income, 38 median age. Stand-up comedy at a premium venue is a natural fit. High adult skew, one-night-only event, and the Roxy is a well-known destination venue. Strong pick for the mix of young professionals and empty nesters in this readership.
